Class CpuFrequencyResidency

java.lang.Object
oshi.driver.common.mac.CpuFrequencyResidency
@ThreadSafe public final class CpuFrequencyResidency extends Object
Derives Apple Silicon CPU frequencies from the performance state residency the IOReport CPU Stats group publishes, and orders that group's channels the way macOS numbers cores.

A core's channel reports how many ticks it spent in each of its performance states since the previous sample. The states are its idle state or states followed by one state per frequency in the cluster's power manager voltage-states table, in the same ascending order, so pairing the two lists gives the frequency the core actually ran at.

    • UNKNOWN_RANK

      public static final int UNKNOWN_RANK
      Rank prefixRank(String) gives to a name that is not a core channel, or that names a core type this release does not know. It orders after every known type, and a caller pairing channels with cores should treat its presence as a chip it cannot interpret rather than assume where such a core belongs.

  • Method Details

    • activeWeightedFrequency

      public static long activeWeightedFrequency(Map<String,Long> stateResidency, long[] table)
      Computes the frequency a core ran at while it was running, as the average of its cluster's frequencies weighted by the time the core spent at each of them.

      Idle residency is excluded rather than weighted at zero, so the result is the frequency the core selected when it had work, which is what Apple's own tooling reports. A core that did not run at all reports the lowest frequency its cluster can run at, which is both the state such a core is parked in and a value that cannot be mistaken for a failure.

      Parameters:
      stateResidency - the ticks the core spent in each state, in channel state order
      table - the frequencies in Hz the core's cluster can run at, in ascending order
      Returns:
      the frequency in Hz, or 0 if the two lists cannot be paired or the core was not observed at all

    • realizedComplexStates

      public static Map<Integer, Map<String,Long>> realizedComplexStates(Map<String, Map<String,Long>> complexStates)
      Collects the state residency of the CPU complexes that report the state the hardware ran at, one entry per core type.

      A core type divided into more than one cluster reports one such channel per cluster. Every cluster of a type runs the same frequency table, so their residency is summed by state, giving the frequency that type ran at over the interval. A channel reporting the state the cores asked for rather than the state they got is ignored, as is one whose states cannot be summed with its siblings' because it does not name them the same way.

      Parameters:
      complexStates - the ticks each complex spent in each state, keyed by channel name
      Returns:
      the summed ticks per state of each core type, keyed by that type's rank as prefixRank(String) gives it, in ascending performance order and in channel state order. A type this release does not know is keyed by UNKNOWN_RANK, so a caller pairing these with cores can tell that the sample holds a type it cannot place.

    • orderChannels

      public static List<String> orderChannels(Collection<String> channelNames)
      Orders CPU core channel names the way macOS numbers logical processors: the least performant core type first, and within one type each die in turn.

    • prefixRank

      public static int prefixRank(String channelName)
      Gets the core type of a channel, as its rank in ascending performance order. Channels sharing a rank are the cores of one type, however many clusters they are divided into.
      Parameters:
      channelName - the channel name
      Returns:
      the rank, or a value ordering after every known core type if the name is not a core channel or names an unrecognized core type

    • alignAtTop

      public static int[] alignAtTop(int itemCount, int classCount)
      Distributes a list of items over the efficiency classes, aligned at the top so that the highest class always gets the last item and a class with no item of its own borrows the nearest one.
      Parameters:
      itemCount - the number of items available, which may be zero
      classCount - the number of efficiency classes, at least 1
      Returns:
      the index into the items for each class, or an empty array if there are no items
